messages:
maria: heads-up — did an int4 bring-up of Hera-7B yesterday. quant conversion went fine but when running long meeting summarization (~3500 tokens) the int4 model starts hallucinating and repeating around token ~2100. short contexts look identical to fp16.

rachel: hmm. were you using our tokenizer mapping or the model's baked vocab? any chance of a token id shift?

maria: used our tokenmap-v3 pipeline. token parity checks showed identical ids. this looks like a runtime mismatch, maybe rotary or projection ordering.

maria: incantation I ran:
```bash
python scripts/convert_model.py --src artifacts/hera_fp16 --dst artifacts/hera_int4 --quant int4 --preserve-embeddings false --proj-order auto
python eval/run_on_task.py --model artifacts/hera_int4 --task long_meeting_summarize --input data/meetings/meet_03_3500.txt
```

sameer: auto proj-order can be risky. Gemma-family forks sometimes expect proj_first vs proj_last. If projection order is off the rotary rotation can be applied to the wrong subspace. Can you dump the model config proj_order and head_dim ordering?

maria: config shows proj_order: 'auto' and head_dim_shape: [64,64,64,64]. i'll force proj_last and re-run. also will dump rotary sin/cos near init and dequantize them.

deploy-bot: Triggered job 8812 on bench-cluster (gpu-pool-dedicated). queued -> running on node-7 (A100).

rachel: also check whether the rotary tables and any headwise_scale are quantized to int8/4. we typically store sin/cos and headwise scales in fp16 — precision loss there causes phase offsets that accumulate with position.

maria: good catch. in my first run I included everything in the aggressive int4 pass. dumping headwise params now.

maria: dump snippet:
```
fp16 headwise_scale (first 4): [1.000000, 0.975000, 1.025000, 1.000000]
int4 dequant headwise_scale: [1.18, 0.86, 0.94, 1.09]
fp16 rotary.sin head0 first8: [0.0000, 0.0157, 0.0314, 0.0471, 0.0628, 0.0785, 0.0942, 0.1099]
int4 dequant rotary.sin head0 first8: [0.0002, 0.0161, 0.0322, 0.0483, 0.0645, 0.0807, 0.0969, 0.1131]
```

sameer: that per-head scale distortion is huge. headwise_scale should be preserved in higher precision or quantized with per-head calibration. when head scales change that alters effective frequency of rotation per head -> leads to phase misalignment and long-context degradation.

rachel: can you compare per-step KL/logit-delta for fp16 vs int4 to find when divergence ramps? tools/logit_delta.py helps. if it ramps slowly with position that's a rotary drift signature.

maria: ran quick logit-delta: position 512 KL=0.07, pos 1024 KL=0.25, pos 2048 KL=1.8. argmax flips jump from 2% -> 30% around 2k. matches observed hallucination point.

anya: agree root cause is headwise_scale quantization. fix plan: 1) update quantize pipeline to --preserve-rotary and --preserve-headwise-scale defaults, 2) add an eval test in onboarding harness for 3k+ token long summaries (assert KL < 0.5 at pos 2k), 3) document proj_order gotchas for Gemma->Qwen/Hera forks.

maria: re-run with rotary and headwise scale preserved (left in fp16) and forced proj_last. new run shows KL@2048=0.12, argmax flips 3.8% — much closer to fp16. summary nearly identical. shipping a patch.

maria: PR opened: https://scm.redwood/PR/3250 — changes quantize defaults, adds long-context regression test, and updates model-onboard checklist about rotary/headwise handling.

sameer: nice. add a short unit in tools/quantize_test.py that synthesizes a small headwise_scale vector and verifies dequantization error < 1e-3 when using preserve flags.

rachel: also add a note to conversion-matrix README: if proj_order was inferred (auto), run tools/headmap_diff.py to verify the mapping between q/k/v layers; mismatches often show as small early diffs that amplify.

maria: will follow up with a sweep across 10 long docs to make sure no variance remains. thanks for the quick triage.

deploy-bot: Job 8812 completed on node-7 (A100). logs: https://logs.redwood/job/8812

maria: marking this thread resolved, will paste sweep results tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
